ratings_why.fun: Lighting a loaded line and watching it go off down the zigzag feels great, and spend-or-hold is a real choice; counting pips on seven units every turn keeps it off an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the threshold spill with once-per-chain on the touching zigzag makes placement, gaps and deaths one fuse, and the Bad Omen fires the same fuse on the enemy's board; no tribe today plays like that.

verdict_why: Three short wording fixes (the Thirty-Two's 'you have', the Piper's attack timing, Ilse's 'had') would leave every card readable; the design itself is ready.

points.text: 'Each other unit you have' could include the hand. Say 'each other unit on your board' if that is meant.
The Piper doesn't say whether each unit attacks the moment it Blurts, mid-chain, or after the chain ends. Mid-chain deaths would cut the wire, so the player needs to know which.
Ilse's 'had 2 Gossip' is unclear once her own Gossip sets off Blurts that bring other units to 2. 'Had 2 Gossip when this started' makes it one clean snapshot.
Show each unit's Blurt number in its pip display (Fips 2, the Speaker 1), so threshold changers read without opening the card.

The Wall-Runner is the only card whose text has no rat in it. Something about the same route along the wall, such as rewarding a chain that runs the whole zigzag end to end, would bring the folk through.

standouts.why: Little Fips, the one who sees the far end, throws the news to the far end: story and job are the same thing, and it reads at a glance.
The Speaker Blurts at 1 and fans out to everyone next to it: the hub who never holds the floor, in one line.
The Piper finally makes the knot move one way, all at once; the hold build's payoff is obvious and dramatic.

weakest.why: A generic Discover payoff with a counting condition; the woodland folk don't come through.
Touching-else-nearest placement plus a per-chain limit is a lot to read for a quiet card.
Reads like a rules clause, and the minute-taker idea barely shows in what it does.

flags.note: 'Each other unit you have': board only, or hand too?
When the triggered attacks happen relative to the rest of the chain.
A fully loaded board may make seven attacks before the enemy acts.
Golden Thirty-Two with the Bellringer under the King uses every text many times a turn; the high roll worth a look.
A Discover most turns once the wire is built is strong economy.
